newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-WESTWOOD BREAKS RECORD TO LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WESTWOOD BREAKS RECORD TO LEAD.

text.p: England's exciting young Lee Westwood broke the Druids Glen course record by one stroke to earn a one-shot first round lead in the Irish Open on Thursday.
Another rising star, Denmark's 1996 rookie of the year Thomas Bjorn, pushed hard to equal Westwood's morning six-under-par 65, only failing by a stroke as he held second place.
Both are close to ensuring Ryder Cup debuts in September against the Americans, with Westwood lying fifth and Bjorn eighth in the table from which the top 10 qualify automatically.

Two more Englishmen share third place on four-under-par, 1991 Ryder Cup player Steve Richardson, the man who made his first 1997 cut last week after 15 successive misses, and the recent European Tournament Players Championship winner, Ross McFarlane.
Two of the favourites for the 125,000 pounds ($209,000) first prize are well in touch. Defending champion Colin Montgomerie is three off the pace with Nick Faldo another stroke back.

Montgomerie and Faldo have both forecast a brilliant future for Westwood, who is looking to better one second place and two thirds so far in Europe this year to add to his maiden success in the 1996 Scandinavian Masters. He won last year's Taiheiyo Masters in Japan and this year's non-European Tour Malaysian Open too.
He set the pace by picking up five strokes over his first five holes and his card included an eagle and five birdies with one dropped shot.
"It is a tough course and obviously I benefitted from a great start," said Westwood. "It's difficult to make a mess after being five-under after five.
"It's nice that senior pros are saying good things about me but it doesn't put me under pressure. I gain confidence from it.

"I could have won three times this year but each time a great player played just that bit better - Olazabal, Langer and Montgomerie - so I know something could happen for me. I just want to keep in contention and hopefully something will fall into place."
Bjorn chased him with five birdies by the 11th before halting his charge.

"I'm playing the sort of golf you need to play to be in the Ryder Cup team at just the right time, hitting 17 greens today and averaging 16 last week," said Bjorn, winner of last year's Loch Lomond Invitational which set up his bid for a Cup place.

Faldo admitted to hitting a few poor shots but getting away with them and the same could be said of Montgomerie, who drove into rough at the 13th but then saw his second shot avoid the water by clipping a tree and finding the green to get away with par.
In the first round last year he ran up a triple bogey on the same hole and lay three-over at that stage before going on to win.
European rankings leader Ian Woosnam posted a 71 but it was not a good day for other senior players.

Spaniard Jose Maria Olazabal had one of his worst rounds since returning from injury layoff, a 74, and there were 75s for European Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros of Spain and Bernhard Langer of Germany.
